lessons.title: Inventory
lessons.summary: Ansible inventory defines managed hosts, groups and associated connection or variable data.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Ansible inventory defines managed hosts, groups and associated connection or variable data.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Static files and dynamic plugins provide targets. Group membership influences variable resolution and play selection. Inspect the resolved inventory before a fleet-wide action so an unexpected group cannot broaden the target set.

lessons.takeaway: Static files and dynamic plugins provide targets. Group membership influences variable resolution and play selection. Inspect the resolved inventory before a fleet-wide action so an unexpected group cannot broaden the target set.

lessons.title: Playbooks
lessons.summary: A playbook describes plays that apply ordered tasks to selected hosts.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A playbook describes plays that apply ordered tasks to selected hosts.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Each play establishes hosts, variables and execution settings; tasks invoke modules. Execution can vary with conditions, handlers and failure strategy. Read the target list and task order before assuming a playbook affects only one service.

lessons.takeaway: Each play establishes hosts, variables and execution settings; tasks invoke modules. Execution can vary with conditions, handlers and failure strategy. Read the target list and task order before assuming a playbook affects only one service.

lessons.title: Modules
lessons.summary: Modules implement individual operations such as managing packages, files or services.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Modules implement individual operations such as managing packages, files or services.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Purpose-built modules often understand desired state and report meaningful changes better than shell commands. Their check-mode and diff support varies. Use module documentation to understand required parameters and side effects.

lessons.takeaway: Purpose-built modules often understand desired state and report meaningful changes better than shell commands. Their check-mode and diff support varies. Use module documentation to understand required parameters and side effects.

lessons.title: Idempotence
lessons.summary: Idempotence means repeating automation with the same desired state should not produce additional unintended changes.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Idempotence means repeating automation with the same desired state should not produce additional unintended changes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Modules compare actual state with requested state where possible. A shell command that always appends a line is not idempotent. Test a second run and inspect changed results rather than treating a successful first run as sufficient.

lessons.takeaway: Modules compare actual state with requested state where possible. A shell command that always appends a line is not idempotent. Test a second run and inspect changed results rather than treating a successful first run as sufficient.

lessons.title: Become
lessons.summary: Privilege escalation lets Ansible perform selected tasks as another user through mechanisms such as sudo.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Privilege escalation lets Ansible perform selected tasks as another user through mechanisms such as sudo.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The SSH connection user and become user are distinct. Apply escalation only where needed and verify the target policy. Broad root execution can hide ownership mistakes and increase the impact of incorrect inventory.

lessons.takeaway: The SSH connection user and become user are distinct. Apply escalation only where needed and verify the target policy. Broad root execution can hide ownership mistakes and increase the impact of incorrect inventory.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.summary: Variables parameterize tasks, templates and roles.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Variables parameterize tasks, templates and roles.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Values can come from inventory, playbooks, roles and runtime inputs with defined precedence. Unexpected overrides often explain environment-specific behavior. Keep sources clear and avoid relying on obscure precedence to encode critical production differences.

lessons.takeaway: Values can come from inventory, playbooks, roles and runtime inputs with defined precedence. Unexpected overrides often explain environment-specific behavior. Keep sources clear and avoid relying on obscure precedence to encode critical production differences.

lessons.title: Facts
lessons.summary: Facts describe information gathered from managed hosts, such as operating system and network details.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Facts describe information gathered from managed hosts, such as operating system and network details.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Fact gathering invokes setup or other collectors and can add overhead. Cached facts may become stale. Use facts for supported platform branching, but verify assumptions before destructive storage or network changes.

lessons.takeaway: Fact gathering invokes setup or other collectors and can add overhead. Cached facts may become stale. Use facts for supported platform branching, but verify assumptions before destructive storage or network changes.

lessons.title: Handlers
lessons.summary: Handlers run actions notified by tasks that report changes.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Handlers run actions notified by tasks that report changes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They usually run at defined flush points and coalesce repeated notifications. This makes a single restart possible after several configuration updates. Failure behavior and force-handlers settings affect whether a notified handler eventually runs.

lessons.takeaway: They usually run at defined flush points and coalesce repeated notifications. This makes a single restart possible after several configuration updates. Failure behavior and force-handlers settings affect whether a notified handler eventually runs.

lessons.title: Check mode
lessons.summary: Check mode asks supported modules to predict changes without applying them.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Check mode asks supported modules to predict changes without applying them.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Not every module supports prediction, and tasks depending on registered results can behave differently. It is a planning aid, not proof that a real run is harmless. Validate in an isolated representative environment as well.

lessons.takeaway: Not every module supports prediction, and tasks depending on registered results can behave differently. It is a planning aid, not proof that a real run is harmless. Validate in an isolated representative environment as well.

lessons.title: Diff mode
lessons.summary: Diff mode displays supported before-and-after changes, especially for text files.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Diff mode displays supported before-and-after changes, especially for text files.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It makes configuration review easier but can expose secrets in templates or file contents. Combine it with check mode where supported and disable diff for sensitive tasks. A diff shows proposed bytes, not application validity.

lessons.takeaway: It makes configuration review easier but can expose secrets in templates or file contents. Combine it with check mode where supported and disable diff for sensitive tasks. A diff shows proposed bytes, not application validity.

lessons.title: Vault
lessons.summary: Ansible Vault encrypts selected files or variable values at rest.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Ansible Vault encrypts selected files or variable values at rest.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Authorized execution decrypts values for use, so logs and generated files still need protection. Separate vault credentials from encrypted data and scope access by environment. Encryption does not replace least privilege on target systems.

lessons.takeaway: Authorized execution decrypts values for use, so logs and generated files still need protection. Separate vault credentials from encrypted data and scope access by environment. Encryption does not replace least privilege on target systems.

lessons.title: Templates
lessons.summary: Templates render configuration files using variables and Jinja expressions.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Templates render configuration files using variables and Jinja expressions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The template module compares rendered output with the destination and can notify handlers on change. Validate generated syntax before replacing a working configuration. Avoid embedding environment-specific secrets in broadly readable artifacts.

lessons.takeaway: The template module compares rendered output with the destination and can notify handlers on change. Validate generated syntax before replacing a working configuration. Avoid embedding environment-specific secrets in broadly readable artifacts.

lessons.title: Roles
lessons.summary: Roles organize reusable tasks, handlers, defaults, variables and files.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Roles organize reusable tasks, handlers, defaults, variables and files.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They provide a conventional structure and an interface through variables. Keep dependencies and assumptions documented so the role can be tested independently. A role should not silently change unrelated system settings.

lessons.takeaway: They provide a conventional structure and an interface through variables. Keep dependencies and assumptions documented so the role can be tested independently. A role should not silently change unrelated system settings.

lessons.title: Collections
lessons.summary: Collections package modules, plugins, roles and documentation under a namespace.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Collections package modules, plugins, roles and documentation under a namespace.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Versioned collection requirements make controller environments reproducible. Pin and review updates because module behavior can change. The controller's installed collection version is part of the automation's effective implementation.

lessons.takeaway: Versioned collection requirements make controller environments reproducible. Pin and review updates because module behavior can change. The controller's installed collection version is part of the automation's effective implementation.

lessons.title: FQCNs
lessons.summary: A fully qualified collection name identifies a plugin or module by namespace and collection.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A fully qualified collection name identifies a plugin or module by namespace and collection.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: For example, ansible.builtin.copy explicitly selects the built-in copy module. Qualification avoids ambiguity when collections provide similarly named plugins and makes documentation lookup clearer.

lessons.takeaway: For example, ansible.builtin.copy explicitly selects the built-in copy module. Qualification avoids ambiguity when collections provide similarly named plugins and makes documentation lookup clearer.

lessons.title: Conditionals
lessons.summary: Conditionals decide whether a task runs for a host based on evaluated data.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Conditionals decide whether a task runs for a host based on evaluated data.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: when expressions can use facts, variables and registered results. Handle undefined values deliberately and avoid assuming string values behave like booleans. A skipped prerequisite may leave later tasks without the data they expect.

lessons.takeaway: when expressions can use facts, variables and registered results. Handle undefined values deliberately and avoid assuming string values behave like booleans. A skipped prerequisite may leave later tasks without the data they expect.

lessons.title: Registered results
lessons.summary: A registered result stores a task's returned fields for later decisions.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A registered result stores a task's returned fields for later decisions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Return structures differ by module; command results often include rc, stdout and stderr. Inspect documented fields before writing conditions. A skipped task or failed command can produce a different result shape.

lessons.takeaway: Return structures differ by module; command results often include rc, stdout and stderr. Inspect documented fields before writing conditions. A skipped task or failed command can produce a different result shape.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.summary: Loops apply a task to a sequence of items.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Loops apply a task to a sequence of items.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Each item produces its own result, and registered loop output contains a results collection. Label loops to keep logs readable and avoid leaking secrets through item values. Repeated service restarts inside loops can often be replaced with a handler.

lessons.takeaway: Each item produces its own result, and registered loop output contains a results collection. Label loops to keep logs readable and avoid leaking secrets through item values. Repeated service restarts inside loops can often be replaced with a handler.

lessons.title: Failure conditions
lessons.summary: failed_when defines which result should count as task failure.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: failed_when defines which result should count as task failure.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Some commands return nonzero statuses for expected conditions, while a zero status may still carry an invalid result. Express the application's actual failure rule. Broad ignore_errors can allow broken prerequisites to cascade into misleading later success.

lessons.takeaway: Some commands return nonzero statuses for expected conditions, while a zero status may still carry an invalid result. Express the application's actual failure rule. Broad ignore_errors can allow broken prerequisites to cascade into misleading later success.

lessons.title: Change reporting
lessons.summary: changed_when defines whether a task reports a state change.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: changed_when defines whether a task reports a state change.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Accurate reporting drives handlers and helps detect drift. Marking every shell task unchanged hides real changes; marking every read-only task changed causes unnecessary restarts. Prefer state-aware modules and define custom conditions where necessary.

lessons.takeaway: Accurate reporting drives handlers and helps detect drift. Marking every shell task unchanged hides real changes; marking every read-only task changed causes unnecessary restarts. Prefer state-aware modules and define custom conditions where necessary.

lessons.title: Serial rollout
lessons.summary: serial limits the number or percentage of hosts processed in each play batch.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: serial limits the number or percentage of hosts processed in each play batch.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Batching preserves capacity during maintenance and lets health gates stop expansion. Verify group size and failure thresholds before use. A batch size of one still needs meaningful validation between hosts.

lessons.takeaway: Batching preserves capacity during maintenance and lets health gates stop expansion. Verify group size and failure thresholds before use. A batch size of one still needs meaningful validation between hosts.

lessons.title: Delegation
lessons.summary: Delegation runs a task on a different host from the play's current target.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Delegation runs a task on a different host from the play's current target.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It supports load-balancer operations or controller-side API calls while iterating application hosts. Variable and connection context need attention, and delegated tasks may still execute concurrently. Protect shared delegated resources from races.

lessons.takeaway: It supports load-balancer operations or controller-side API calls while iterating application hosts. Variable and connection context need attention, and delegated tasks may still execute concurrently. Protect shared delegated resources from races.

lessons.title: Run once
lessons.summary: run_once schedules a task once for the applicable execution batch rather than for every host.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: run_once schedules a task once for the applicable execution batch rather than for every host.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: With serial execution, it can run once per batch. Host-dependent conditions and variables may come from the selected host. Use a dedicated play or explicit coordination when an operation must occur exactly once across an entire deployment.

lessons.takeaway: With serial execution, it can run once per batch. Host-dependent conditions and variables may come from the selected host. Use a dedicated play or explicit coordination when an operation must occur exactly once across an entire deployment.

lessons.title: Blocks and rescue
lessons.summary: Blocks group tasks and attach shared settings, rescue handling and cleanup behavior.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Blocks group tasks and attach shared settings, rescue handling and cleanup behavior.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A rescue section can handle qualifying task failures; always can perform cleanup. Unreachable hosts and some invalid task definitions do not behave like ordinary task failures. Recovery must still verify whether partially applied changes remain.

lessons.takeaway: A rescue section can handle qualifying task failures; always can perform cleanup. Unreachable hosts and some invalid task definitions do not behave like ordinary task failures. Recovery must still verify whether partially applied changes remain.

lessons.title: Async tasks
lessons.summary: Async execution lets long-running tasks continue beyond the normal synchronous task duration.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Async execution lets long-running tasks continue beyond the normal synchronous task duration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: poll controls waiting behavior and async sets a time bound. With poll zero, follow up using async_status rather than assuming completion. Avoid launching unbounded concurrent work against a shared dependency.

lessons.takeaway: poll controls waiting behavior and async sets a time bound. With poll zero, follow up using async_status rather than assuming completion. Avoid launching unbounded concurrent work against a shared dependency.

lessons.title: Tags
lessons.summary: Tags select subsets of tasks for execution.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Tags select subsets of tasks for execution.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They speed focused operations but may skip prerequisites or validation. Document supported tag combinations and test them. A tagged task can still depend on variables or facts normally prepared by omitted tasks.

lessons.takeaway: They speed focused operations but may skip prerequisites or validation. Document supported tag combinations and test them. A tagged task can still depend on variables or facts normally prepared by omitted tasks.

lessons.title: Dynamic inventory
lessons.summary: Dynamic inventory discovers hosts from external systems through plugins.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Dynamic inventory discovers hosts from external systems through plugins.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The resulting membership can change between runs, so verify the target snapshot and filtering rules. Credentials, caching and naming conventions affect correctness. A discovery API failure must not silently become an unintended empty or broad deployment.

lessons.takeaway: The resulting membership can change between runs, so verify the target snapshot and filtering rules. Credentials, caching and naming conventions affect correctness. A discovery API failure must not silently become an unintended empty or broad deployment.

lessons.title: Concurrency
lessons.summary: Ansible concurrency determines how many hosts and tasks can progress simultaneously.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Ansible concurrency determines how many hosts and tasks can progress simultaneously.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: forks, serial, throttle and strategy settings control different dimensions. More concurrency can overwhelm package mirrors, APIs or shared databases. Choose limits from dependency capacity and deployment failure domains.

lessons.takeaway: forks, serial, throttle and strategy settings control different dimensions. More concurrency can overwhelm package mirrors, APIs or shared databases. Choose limits from dependency capacity and deployment failure domains.

lessons.title: Secret logging
lessons.summary: Automation can expose sensitive values in task arguments, diffs, registered results or debug output.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Automation can expose sensitive values in task arguments, diffs, registered results or debug output.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: no_log suppresses selected task output but does not secure every downstream use or generated file. Keep secrets out of loop labels and broad debug dumps. Protect controller logs and target-file permissions.

lessons.takeaway: no_log suppresses selected task output but does not secure every downstream use or generated file. Keep secrets out of loop labels and broad debug dumps. Protect controller logs and target-file permissions.

lessons.title: Automation validation
lessons.summary: Validation checks syntax, targets, rendered configuration and runtime behavior before broad execution.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Validation checks syntax, targets, rendered configuration and runtime behavior before broad execution.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Combine syntax checks, inventory review, supported check mode and a representative test host. Run twice to assess idempotence and verify application health after changes. A syntax-valid playbook can still target the wrong machines.

lessons.takeaway: Combine syntax checks, inventory review, supported check mode and a representative test host. Run twice to assess idempotence and verify application health after changes. A syntax-valid playbook can still target the wrong machines.

commands.title: Inventory graph
commands.definition: Resolves inventory and displays group membership.
commands.purpose: Review the exact fleet before running a play.
commands.environment: Read-only discovery may call external inventory APIs; inspect a trusted inventory source.
commands.interpretation: Group branches show membership; unexpected hosts indicate inventory or filter problems.
commands.safety: Read-only discovery may call external inventory APIs; inspect a trusted inventory source.

commands.title: Host variables
commands.definition: Prints resolved inventory variables for one host.
commands.purpose: Find connection settings or unexpected variable values.
commands.environment: Can reveal secrets; replace HOST and protect output.
commands.interpretation: JSON keys show inventory-derived values, not every later play-level override.
commands.safety: Can reveal secrets; replace HOST and protect output.

commands.title: List play targets
commands.definition: Lists hosts matched by each play without executing its tasks.
commands.purpose: Verify host patterns and limits before changes.
commands.environment: Inventory plugins may execute discovery; use trusted project files.
commands.interpretation: Read the play name, pattern and host count for every play.
commands.safety: Inventory plugins may execute discovery; use trusted project files.

commands.title: List tasks
commands.definition: Shows statically discoverable tasks selected by a playbook.
commands.purpose: Review order and scope before execution.
commands.environment: Does not execute normal tasks; not a complete prediction of dynamic behavior.
commands.interpretation: Dynamic includes may not expose every eventual task in this view.
commands.safety: Does not execute normal tasks; not a complete prediction of dynamic behavior.

commands.title: Syntax validation
commands.definition: Parses and checks playbook syntax.
commands.purpose: Catch malformed YAML and structural issues early.
commands.environment: Does not validate every runtime variable, remote command or application configuration.
commands.interpretation: Success normally prints the playbook name; failures identify parsing context.
commands.safety: Does not validate every runtime variable, remote command or application configuration.

commands.title: Check mode
commands.definition: Requests predicted changes on a limited target set.
commands.purpose: Preview supported operations before a real rollout.
commands.environment: Not a universal dry run; modules and tasks can have exceptions, so review trusted content and use a safe canary.
commands.interpretation: changed means a predicted change for supporting modules; skipped tasks may reduce coverage.
commands.safety: Not a universal dry run; modules and tasks can have exceptions, so review trusted content and use a safe canary.

commands.title: Check with diff
commands.definition: Adds supported before/after diffs to check-mode output.
commands.purpose: Review rendered configuration changes.
commands.environment: Diffs can expose secrets; disable diff on sensitive tasks.
commands.interpretation: Lines prefixed - are removed and + are added; inspect paths and values.
commands.safety: Diffs can expose secrets; disable diff on sensitive tasks.

commands.title: Module documentation
commands.definition: Displays the installed module's options, behavior and examples.
commands.purpose: Confirm parameters and check-mode support for the actual installed version.
commands.environment: Local read-only documentation lookup.
commands.interpretation: Read required fields, attributes and return values before using conditions.
commands.safety: Local read-only documentation lookup.

commands.title: Collection versions
commands.definition: Lists installed collections and versions.
commands.purpose: Reproduce a controller environment and diagnose version differences.
commands.environment: Read-only; compare with project requirements.
commands.interpretation: Multiple installation paths may contain different versions; note the path headings.
commands.safety: Read-only; compare with project requirements.

commands.title: Connectivity test
commands.definition: Tests Ansible connection and Python execution on selected hosts.
commands.purpose: Distinguish transport or interpreter problems from playbook logic.
commands.environment: Not ICMP ping; runs a module on the authorized target.
commands.interpretation: pong means module execution succeeded; unreachable indicates connection-level failure.
commands.safety: Not ICMP ping; runs a module on the authorized target.

commands.title: Gather selected facts
commands.definition: Collects filtered operating-system facts.
commands.purpose: Check platform assumptions used by roles.
commands.environment: Runs read-oriented fact gathering remotely; scope targets and protect inventory details.
commands.interpretation: Returned ansible_facts show distribution and version fields available on the host.
commands.safety: Runs read-oriented fact gathering remotely; scope targets and protect inventory details.

commands.title: List tags
commands.definition: Shows tags available for task selection.
commands.purpose: Understand supported partial-run entry points.
commands.environment: Read-only task discovery; test tag combinations before production use.
commands.interpretation: TASK TAGS identifies selectable labels; dependencies may still be omitted by selective execution.
commands.safety: Read-only task discovery; test tag combinations before production use.

commands.title: Ansible version and paths
commands.definition: Reports ansible-core version and active configuration paths.
commands.purpose: Reproduce differences between a developer workstation and CI.
commands.environment: Read-only; does not contact inventory hosts.
commands.interpretation: config file, module paths and Python version explain the controller environment.
commands.safety: Read-only; does not contact inventory hosts.

references.title: Ansible version and paths — primary documentation

commands.title: Changed configuration settings
commands.definition: Displays non-default effective Ansible configuration.
commands.purpose: Find an unexpected inventory, connection or privilege setting.
commands.environment: Read-only controller inspection; output can expose internal paths or configuration values.
commands.interpretation: Entries show setting names and origins where supported; environment variables can override file values.
commands.safety: Read-only controller inspection; output can expose internal paths or configuration values.

commands.title: Configuration source file
commands.definition: Prints the active Ansible configuration file.
commands.purpose: Inspect project configuration without guessing which file is in use.
commands.environment: Read-only; configuration may include sensitive paths or plugin settings.
commands.interpretation: This is file content, not every resolved environment override; compare with dump for effective values.
commands.safety: Read-only; configuration may include sensitive paths or plugin settings.

commands.title: Full resolved inventory
commands.definition: Outputs resolved inventory as structured JSON.
commands.purpose: Inspect groups and host variables before applying a play.
commands.environment: Read-only host inspection, but inventory plugins can call external APIs; protect exported variables.
commands.interpretation: _meta.hostvars contains host variables; groups contain hosts and children. Dynamically supplied variables may include secrets.
commands.safety: Read-only host inspection, but inventory plugins can call external APIs; protect exported variables.

commands.title: Host pattern preview
commands.definition: Shows hosts matching the intersection of two groups.
commands.purpose: Validate a narrowed target pattern before remote execution.
commands.environment: Read-only inventory resolution; keep the shell quotes around the pattern.
commands.interpretation: The count and names are the resolved target set; group names alone are not an access control.
commands.safety: Read-only inventory resolution; keep the shell quotes around the pattern.

commands.title: Module inventory
commands.definition: Lists modules discoverable by the controller.
commands.purpose: Find available modules and identify missing collections.
commands.environment: Read-only; collection paths and versions affect results.
commands.expectedOutput: ansible.builtin.copy Copy files to remote locations
commands.interpretation: Each line names a module and brief description; presence does not guarantee remote requirements are installed.
commands.safety: Read-only; collection paths and versions affect results.

commands.title: Module task examples
commands.definition: Prints a task-oriented parameter skeleton for a module.
commands.purpose: Start from documented parameter names rather than guessing syntax.
commands.environment: Read-only; a generated snippet is not a tested production task.
commands.interpretation: Commented fields describe options; required fields must still be supplied and examples reviewed.
commands.safety: Read-only; a generated snippet is not a tested production task.

commands.title: Collection installation
commands.definition: Installs collections declared in a requirements file.
commands.purpose: Reproduce reviewed automation dependencies on a clean controller.
commands.environment: Downloads executable automation content; use reviewed trusted collections and version constraints.
commands.interpretation: Installation messages name collection versions and destination paths; inspect the requirements file for intended pins.
commands.safety: Downloads executable automation content; use reviewed trusted collections and version constraints.

commands.title: Collection metadata
commands.definition: Emits installed collection versions as JSON.
commands.purpose: Record the automation toolchain in a CI diagnostic artifact.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect actual search order if duplicate versions exist.
commands.interpretation: Paths group installed collections and their versions; multiple paths may contain different versions.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect actual search order if duplicate versions exist.

commands.title: Role installation
commands.definition: Installs role dependencies from a declared requirements file.
commands.purpose: Set up a reproducible role-based project.
commands.environment: Downloads executable task content; use reviewed sources and pins.
commands.interpretation: Messages identify installed role versions or revisions; an unpinned source can change later.
commands.safety: Downloads executable task content; use reviewed sources and pins.

commands.title: Encrypt a variable file
commands.definition: Encrypts a plaintext variable file with Vault.
commands.purpose: Protect stored secret content before committing it.
commands.environment: Mutates the file and prompts for a Vault secret. Keep secure recovery access and rotate already-exposed credentials.
commands.interpretation: The encrypted file begins with a Vault header; successful encryption does not remove prior plaintext history or logs.
commands.safety: Mutates the file and prompts for a Vault secret. Keep secure recovery access and rotate already-exposed credentials.

references.title: Encrypt a variable file — primary documentation

commands.title: View encrypted content
commands.definition: Decrypts a Vault file for display without rewriting it.
commands.purpose: Inspect authorized secret content when necessary.
commands.environment: Sensitive read; use a private terminal and never redirect the output into shared CI logs.
commands.expectedOutput: Decrypted YAML displayed on the terminal
commands.interpretation: Output is plaintext, not masked values; the command's success only confirms decryption.
commands.safety: Sensitive read; use a private terminal and never redirect the output into shared CI logs.

commands.title: Edit encrypted content
commands.definition: Opens decrypted content in an editor and re-encrypts on save.
commands.purpose: Maintain an authorized Vault-protected variable file.
commands.environment: Mutates secrets; secure editor swap/backup handling and use the intended Vault identity.
commands.expectedOutput: Vault file saved after editor exit
commands.interpretation: The editor shows plaintext during editing; inspect the final file header after saving.
commands.safety: Mutates secrets; secure editor swap/backup handling and use the intended Vault identity.

commands.title: Change Vault encryption key
commands.definition: Re-encrypts a Vault file using a new Vault secret.
commands.purpose: Rotate access to stored encrypted content.
commands.environment: Mutates encryption; update authorized consumers securely and preserve a recovery path.
commands.interpretation: Rekey successful refers to the file encryption key, not the application credentials stored inside.
commands.safety: Mutates encryption; update authorized consumers securely and preserve a recovery path.

references.title: Change Vault encryption key — primary documentation

commands.title: Canary execution
commands.definition: Runs the playbook on the explicitly limited host pattern.
commands.purpose: Apply a reviewed change to a small representative target set.
commands.environment: Mutates remote hosts according to all selected tasks. Preview hosts and check availability before execution.
commands.interpretation: PLAY RECAP shows ok, changed, unreachable and failed; zero failed is not a substitute for service postconditions.
commands.safety: Mutates remote hosts according to all selected tasks. Preview hosts and check availability before execution.

commands.title: Privilege-scoped execution
commands.definition: Runs a reviewed maintenance play and prompts for an escalation password where become is configured.
commands.purpose: Use an interactive authorized privilege path without putting passwords in shell arguments.
commands.environment: May change privileged host state. Use task-scoped become and protect the interactive session.
commands.interpretation: Escalation applies according to the play/task settings; a prompt does not mean every task should run as root.
commands.safety: May change privileged host state. Use task-scoped become and protect the interactive session.

commands.title: Validate tagged path
commands.definition: Lists tasks selected for a tagged execution path.
commands.purpose: Check whether prerequisites are omitted before a partial rollout.
commands.environment: Read-only planning aid; test the selected path in a representative environment.
commands.interpretation: The task list reflects tag selection; dynamic includes may not reveal every runtime task in this preview.
commands.safety: Read-only planning aid; test the selected path in a representative environment.

commands.title: Read-only remote command
commands.definition: Runs uptime on a deliberately scoped remote target.
commands.purpose: Verify connection context and inspect current load without a shell pipeline.
commands.environment: Connects to hosts; the example is read-only, but command can execute arbitrary actions. Use a verified host pattern.
commands.interpretation: stdout contains remote uptime/load; Ansible command may report CHANGED despite this command being observational.

debugging.title: Unexpected deployment targets
debugging.symptom: A playbook resolves more hosts than the operator intended.

steps.evidence: Inspect group membership, inventory plugins and host-pattern expansion. Confirm limits apply to every relevant play.
Stop before execution and correct inventory filters or the host pattern. Use a verified canary subset before broader batches.
Repeat target listing and confirm exact expected hosts, then verify no unrelated hosts changed after rollout.

debugging.title: Every run reports changes
debugging.symptom: A configuration play reports changed on every execution despite stable desired state.

steps.evidence: Identify tasks with nondeterministic template values or shell commands lacking state-aware conditions. Distinguish reporting errors from actual repeated writes.
Use purpose-built modules, stable templates and accurate changed_when rules. Do not mark real changes unchanged merely to make the recap green.
Run twice on a test host; the second run should show no unintended changes or restarts while deliberate drift is still corrected.

debugging.title: Handler never restarts service
debugging.symptom: A configuration file changes but the service keeps old behavior.

steps.evidence: Check notify names, task changed status, handler scope and earlier failures. A handler may not run after a later failure under default behavior.
Correct notification wiring and validate configuration before restart. Choose failure/handler behavior deliberately rather than forcing every handler unconditionally.
Change a harmless test setting and confirm one restart or reload occurs and the application uses the new configuration.

debugging.title: Check mode misses a failure
debugging.symptom: A dry run passes but the real deployment fails on a dependent task.

steps.evidence: Review module check-mode support and tasks that depend on registered results or resources not created during check mode.
Add representative integration tests and explicit validation for the dependency. Treat check mode as one signal rather than the sole gate.
Run the real workflow on an isolated canary and test both the first and second execution before promotion.

debugging.title: Secret appears in output
debugging.symptom: A failed template task prints a credential into the CI log.

steps.evidence: Trace where the secret entered task arguments, diffs, debug output or loop labels. Identify log readers and retained artifacts.
Rotate the exposed value, restrict affected logs and add no_log or diff suppression where needed. Secure generated files as well as controller output.
Use a nonproduction sentinel secret in a controlled test and confirm it does not appear in logs or artifacts.

references.title: Secret appears in output — primary documentation

debugging.title: Variable unexpectedly overridden
debugging.symptom: A role uses a production endpoint during a staging run.

steps.evidence: Compare inventory variables with role defaults, play vars and runtime extra variables. Inventory output alone does not show every precedence source.
Remove ambiguous overrides and make environment inputs explicit. Add assertions for expected environment and endpoint before mutation.
Render and validate configuration for each environment and verify the effective endpoint on the canary.

debugging.title: Rolling update removes too much capacity
debugging.symptom: A service becomes unavailable during a fleet play.

steps.evidence: Inspect serial, forks, strategy and health checks. Confirm the batch size relative to replica count and failure domains.
Stop expansion, restore healthy capacity and reduce batch size. Gate each batch on application readiness and dependency capacity.
Run a controlled rollout and verify minimum serving capacity and user success remain within the objective throughout.

references.title: Rolling update removes too much capacity — primary documentation

debugging.title: Privilege escalation fails
debugging.symptom: SSH connectivity works but privileged tasks fail.

steps.evidence: Separate connection identity from become identity and inspect the actual sudo policy and error. Connectivity success does not prove escalation rights.
Grant the narrowly required escalation or adjust task scope to avoid unnecessary privilege. Do not default every role to unrestricted root.
Test the required privileged operation and confirm unrelated privileged operations remain denied.

debugging.title: Run-once migration repeats
debugging.symptom: A database migration runs more than once during a serial deployment.

steps.evidence: Check whether run_once is evaluated once per serial batch and whether delegation causes shared-target concurrency.
Move the migration to an explicitly coordinated stage or dedicated play and make it idempotent. Protect it with an application-level migration lock where appropriate.
Test multiple batches and verify exactly the intended migration outcome with safe handling of retries.

debugging.title: Partial configuration after failure
debugging.symptom: A play changes several files and then fails before validation completes.

steps.evidence: Inspect which tasks completed and actual target state. Rescue behavior is not a transaction rollback, and unreachable hosts need separate handling.
Restore a known-good configuration or complete a controlled forward repair, then improve validation-before-activation and recovery blocks.
Verify application health and a clean repeat run on affected hosts before continuing the fleet.
